comment: Proposed buildings do not show measured clearance dimensions from the outside conductor of overhead electric lines. All buildings with potential clearance concerns require clearance dimension annotations on site plan and building elevation sheets, measured from the outside (outermost) conductor, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance is maintained per UCM § 1.10.3.
applicableAreas: Buildings and permanent structures throughout the site
observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) clearly shows overhead utility lines (O.H.U.L.) running along Valley View Road (western boundary) and the northern property boundary, with utility poles marked. The proposed site plan (Sheet 9) shows eight multi-story residential buildings (ranging from 33'-5" to 36'-1" in height) positioned on the site. The overhead electric utility line is labeled '----OHE----' on the site plan running along the Valley View Road frontage (southern boundary). However, NO clearance dimensions are annotated anywhere on Sheet 9 showing the horizontal distance from the outside conductor of the overhead line to any building face or structure. No building elevation sheets with surveyed conductor locations and clearance dimensions were found in the submitted plans.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires buildings to maintain a minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead primary, neutral, and secondary conductors. The regulation defines this as a vertical plane extending infinitely upward from a point 7.5 feet from the conductor. The site plan shows buildings within reasonable proximity to the overhead lines along Valley View Road, but the applicant has provided no dimensional evidence that the 7.5-foot minimum horizontal clearance is maintained. The absence of clearance annotations and dimensions constitutes a failure to demonstrate compliance. Per the grouping documentation, clearance dimensions must be labeled on plans with dimension lines originating from the actual outside conductor location (not pole centerline).

comment: Building elevation sheets do not show surveyed elevations of existing overhead electric conductors. Sealed building elevation exhibits are required for all buildings with potential proximity to overhead lines, showing the surveyed elevation of the outside conductor and dimensioned clearances from the conductor to building faces and projections.
observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) documents existing overhead utility lines running along the property boundary and service drop. The proposed buildings range from 33'-4.75" to 36'-1" in height. A complete set of building elevation sheets showing the surveyed elevation of the existing overhead conductors is not present in the submitted site plan set. While general notes on Sheet 3 reference benchmarks (B.M. #1 at 678.52' and B.M. #2 at 681.08' NAVD 88), these are general site control points, not surveyed overhead conductor elevations. No building elevation exhibits were found that show the actual conductor elevation overlaid with the building profile to verify vertical clearances.
reasoning: Per the grouping's Documentation Requirements section, 'Profile plans: Engineered, sealed profile drawings showing vertical relationships between overhead conductors and building features, including overhangs, balconies, and canopies, with dimensioned clearances' are required. The grouping cites UCM § 1.10.3 as requiring permanent clearances and explicitly states that clearance verification requires 'surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors included on building elevation sheets.' Without surveyed conductor elevation data on building elevation sheets, the applicant cannot demonstrate that the 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance or other required clearances are met.

comment: Section and plan view exhibits do not show dimensions from the outside electric conductor to the outermost edges of proposed buildings, building projections, and other site features. Enlarged plan details and section views are required showing dimension lines originating from the outside conductor and extending to all building faces and structures within potential clearance distance, demonstrating compliance with the 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance requirement.
applicableAreas: Site plan sections and elevation views
observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) clearly identifies overhead utility lines with the notation 'O.H.U.L.' running along Valley View Road and the northern property boundary. The proposed site plan (Sheet 9) and landscape plan (Sheet 31) both show overhead electric lines (labeled 'OHE' or '----OHE----') but NO dimension lines or clearance annotations extending from the outside conductor to the outer edges of any buildings, projections, site features, or structures. No section views or profile exhibits were found showing the cross-section relationship between the overhead conductor and site features. The landscape plan shows trees proposed near the OHE line but with no distance callouts or species specifications.
reasoning: The grouping explicitly states: 'Common Violation Patterns: Clearances measured from pole instead of conductor... Dimension annotations read "10'-0" from pole" instead of "15'-0" from outside conductor"' and 'Missing profile plans: Site plan shows building and overhead lines in plan view only, no elevation/section view; no surveyed mid-span clearance data; cannot verify vertical clearances meet requirements.' UCM § 1.10.3 requires permanent clearances, which must be demonstrated through dimension callouts showing measurement from the outside (outermost) conductor to the building edge. The complete absence of these dimensions constitutes a deficiency.

comment: The proposed driveway crosses the existing overhead electric line at Valley View Road. No section views, surveyed mid-span clearance measurements, or vertical clearance dimension annotations are provided to demonstrate the minimum 16-foot (or 18-foot for truck traffic areas) vertical clearance from the lowest point of the overhead line to the finished driveway grade. A registered surveyor's survey showing mid-span clearance is required, with results documented on section views and profile sheets.
applicableAreas: Proposed driveway intersection with overhead utility line at Valley View Road frontage
observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows an overhead utility line labeled 'O.H.U.L.' running along Valley View Road (western boundary). The proposed site plan (Sheet 9) shows a proposed driveway at the bottom left (Valley View Road frontage) area. Per the vision analysis of Sheet 9, the proposed driveway 'crosses directly under the horizontal ----OHE---- line' along Valley View Road. The grading plan (Sheet 11) shows the finished floor elevations and site grades but does not annotate the vertical clearance dimensions at the driveway location where the overhead line crosses. No registered surveyor data showing mid-span clearance measurements is provided. The roadway grade elevations are not dimensioned relative to the overhead line height.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.6.2 specifies: 'Driveway and parking without truck traffic: 16 feet minimum vertical clearance; Roads, streets, alleys, and areas with truck traffic: 18 feet minimum vertical clearance from lowest point of overhead electric facilities including telecommunications attachments.' The grouping documentation notes this is a 'Common Violation Pattern: Inadequate service-drop clearances: Driveway grade shown within 15-16 feet of overhead service drop without mid-span clearance verification; service drop sag at maximum load/temperature may contact vehicles.' Since the proposed driveway crosses under the overhead line, vertical clearance must be verified through surveyed mid-span clearance data showing the lowest point of the conductor at maximum sag. The absence of this documentation constitutes a failure to demonstrate compliance.

comment: Clearance dimensions are not shown on any plan sheets. When clearance dimensions are eventually provided, they must originate from the outside (outermost) conductor, not from the utility pole centerline. Dimension lines should clearly identify the conductor location and show measurement to the building edge or feature being evaluated.
applicableAreas: All clearance dimension annotations on site plan
observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows multiple utility poles and overhead utility lines (O.H.U.L.) on the property. The proposed site plan (Sheet 9) shows the overhead electric line (OHE) running along the Valley View Road frontage. However, NO clearance dimensions are annotated anywhere on the plans. The grouping documentation emphasizes that 'All clearances must be measured from the outside conductor (the actual electric wire), never from the utility pole centerline or pole structure' and warns that 'Measuring from pole centerline instead of the conductor results in understated clearances and code violations.' Since no dimensions are shown on the plans at all, there is no evidence that the applicant is measuring from the outside conductor versus the pole.
reasoning: Per the grouping's Measurement Methodology section: 'Profile plans must show dimension lines originating at the conductor location, not at the pole. [This is critical.]' The complete absence of clearance dimensions means there is no opportunity to verify that dimensions originate from the conductor rather than the pole. This is a fundamental documentation failure that prevents verification of compliance. Without at least one dimension showing the measurement methodology and origin point (outside conductor), compliance cannot be verified.

comment: The landscape plan shows trees proposed near overhead electric distribution lines but does not identify the botanical species for trees in proximity to the OHE line or provide distance annotations showing lateral clearances. Landscape plan must be revised to: (1) call out the specific tree species being planted in areas near the overhead line (refer to tree species list on Sheet 35), (2) show lateral distance dimensions from proposed trees to the outside conductor, (3) confirm that any trees within 10 feet of the overhead distribution conductor are from the Utility Compatible trees list per ECM Appendix F, or (4) demonstrate all proposed trees are planted beyond the 10-foot clearance zone.
applicableAreas: Landscape plantings near overhead distribution conductors at Valley View Road frontage and site perimeter
observation: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) depicts the overhead electric (OHE) utility line running along the southern/Valley View Road boundary. The vision analysis of Sheet 31 confirms that 'There are several proposed trees located along the bottom boundary line, in close proximity to the -OHE- line' and notes that trees are marked with functional type codes (M for mitigation tree, PL for parking lot tree, P for parking buffer point tree). However, 'Specific botanical species are not labeled on this sheet' and 'There are no specific dimensions or distance callouts explicitly stating the distance from these trees to the overhead electric line.' The landscape calculations sheet (Sheet 35) shows proposed plantings: Cedar Elm (10 trees), Live Oak (2 trees), Mexican Redbud (6 trees), Texas Mountain Laurel (2 trees), and various shrubs and groundcover. However, there is no cross-reference between the species list and the landscape plan to identify which species are being planted near the overhead lines, nor is there any notation confirming these species are Utility Compatible (UC) per ECM Appendix F.
reasoning: The grouping states: 'Trees within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors are from Utility Compatible Shade Trees list' and 'ECM Appendix F "UC" column (utility-compatible trees generally mature height ≤20 feet marked "UC").' The grouping further notes: 'Common Violation Pattern: Non-utility-compatible trees beneath lines: Landscape plan shows large trees beneath or within 10 feet of overhead lines; species not from Utility Compatible list in ECM Appendix F.' The landscape plan fails to: (1) identify which specific proposed tree species are located within 10 feet of the overhead distribution line, (2) provide distance callouts showing lateral distance from proposed trees to the conductor, and (3) confirm that any trees within 10 feet are marked as Utility Compatible in ECM Appendix F. Without this information, compliance cannot be verified.

comment: Plans do not include required note stating that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead electric lines per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003. Add this requirement to the cover sheet general notes or site plan release notes in a location where all contractors and the owner will see it during project execution.
applicableAreas: General notes on cover sheet or site plan sheets
observation: The cover sheet (Sheet 1) and general notes sheet (Sheet 3) were reviewed in detail. Sheet 1 contains standard project information, Fire Department requirements, and administrative notes, but no mention of a 48-hour notification requirement to Austin Energy. Sheet 3 contains comprehensive notes about utilities, construction sequence, benchmarks, fire department requirements, and electric transmission clearances, but no explicit note requiring the owner/contractor to notify Austin Energy 48 hours before work near high-voltage overhead lines. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) similarly contains site plan release notes but no mention of the 48-hour notification requirement. While Sheet 9's release notes (Block 7) reference general utility relocation responsibility (Item 4: 'The owner is responsible for all costs of relocation of, or damage to, utilities' and Item 5: 'Additional electric easements may be required at a later date'), there is no specific note stating that 'owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines' as required by Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003.
reasoning: The grouping's Documentation Requirements section explicitly states: '48-hour notification plan note: Plans must include note that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines (Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003).' The grouping further lists under Common Violation Patterns: 'Missing 48-hour notification note: Site has overhead lines and construction staging area adjacent, but no plan notes addressing notification requirement.' Since overhead electric facilities clearly exist on and adjacent to this site, and construction is planned adjacent to these lines, the required notification note must be prominently displayed on the plans.

comment: Three mitigation trees shown on landscape plan less than 15 feet from overhead electric line lack species identification, preventing verification of utility-compatibility per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Provide species identification for all trees proposed near overhead electric facilities and verify utility-compatible (UC) designation from ECM Appendix F for non-UC tree species.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along overhead electric line
observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows three mitigation trees (marked 'M') positioned in the southeast corner with canopy edges less than 15 feet from the existing OHE (overhead electric) line running along the southern property boundary (per vision analysis). Sheet 35 (Landscape Calculations) provides the plant schedule identifying four tree species proposed: Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, and Mexican Redbud. However, the landscape plan does not identify which species corresponds to the three trees shown near the OHE line. The plans show no clearance measurements or documentation of utility-compatibility verification. Without species identification of the trees near the OHE line and without confirmation that they are utility-compatible (UC per ECM Appendix F), compliance with the 15-foot minimum clearance requirement for non-UC trees from distribution conductors cannot be verified.
reasoning: The grouping requires that non-utility-compatible trees must be at least 15 feet from distribution conductors. The vision analysis clearly shows tree canopy symbols less than 15 feet from the OHE line. The plant schedule lists multiple proposed tree species, some of which (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Mexican Redbud) are not identified in the grouping guidance as utility-compatible species. The critical issue is that the three specific trees shown near the OHE line on the landscape plan are not identified by species, making it impossible to determine their utility-compatibility status. This prevents a definitive pass/fail determination - the deficiency could exist if these trees are non-UC species, but cannot be confirmed without species identification.

comment: Three mitigation trees shown less than 15 feet from overhead electric line lack species identification and mature height confirmation, preventing verification of large-tree clearance requirement (minimum 25 feet from distribution conductors). Identify tree species and provide mature heights per ECM Appendix F for all trees proposed near overhead electric facilities.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along overhead electric line, southeast corner
observation: Sheet 31 shows three mitigation trees in the southeast corner with tree canopy edges positioned less than 15 feet from the OHE line. Sheet 35 plant schedule lists proposed trees including 2 Live Oak (Quercus virginiana) and 10 Cedar Elm (Ulmus crassifolia), both of which typically have mature heights of 40 feet or greater per standard horticultural references and the grouping's example that 'Live Oak Plateau shown as 35 ft when Appendix F specifies 40 ft.' However, the landscape plan does not identify which species the three trees near the OHE line represent. The specification on Sheet 35 lists only container heights at planting (16' minimum for Live Oak and Cedar Elm containers), not mature heights. Planting specifications do not confirm whether the specific trees shown near the OHE are large trees (40+ ft mature height per ECM Appendix F).
reasoning: Large trees (40+ feet mature height per ECM Appendix F) must be more than 25 feet from distribution conductors per UCM § 1.10.10.4. If the three trees positioned less than 15 feet from the OHE line are Live Oak or Cedar Elm (both likely 40+ ft mature height), they would violate this requirement. However, the landscape plan does not identify these specific trees by species, and the plant schedule provides only container sizes and planting heights, not mature heights per ECM Appendix F. Without confirmed species identification of the trees near the OHE and without confirmed mature height designations from ECM Appendix F, a definitive determination cannot be made. The status is unclear rather than fail because the identification could resolve the issue (e.g., if the three trees are Texas Mountain Laurel at 25 ft or Mexican Redbud at 20-30 ft, they would comply).

comment: Trees shown near overhead electric line on landscape plan lack species identification. Provide species labels (common and/or botanical names) directly on the landscape plan for all trees proposed near overhead and underground electric facilities, or provide a clear cross-reference between tree symbols on the landscape plan and species listed in the plant schedule.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along overhead electric line (near OHE); areas throughout site with trees near proposed or existing electric infrastructure
observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows trees near the overhead electric (OHE) line running along the southern boundary. The vision analysis identified three mitigation trees ('M' label) in the southeast corner positioned less than 15 feet from the OHE line. These three trees have no species identification on the landscape plan - they are shown only as generic circular tree symbols with an 'M' label. The landscape plan key notes define tree types by designation (SY, PL, P, M) but do not cross-reference specific species. Sheet 35 provides a plant schedule with species names (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) and quantities, but does not indicate which symbol on the landscape plan corresponds to which species. The common and scientific names are listed in the schedule, but there is no visible link connecting those names to the specific trees shown near the overhead electric line on Sheet 31.
reasoning: Per Reviewer Convention, a plant legend or plant schedule must identify the species of trees proposed near electric facilities to allow verification of clearance requirements and utility-compatibility. The landscape plan shows trees near the OHE line but fails to identify their species by either common name or botanical designation. While the plant schedule exists separately on Sheet 35, it does not clearly indicate which species are the three trees near the OHE line. This creates ambiguity about which trees are which species, making compliance verification impossible. The grouping guidance states that species identification is necessary to verify utility-compatibility against ECM Appendix F and to determine if trees are large trees (40+ ft) requiring special clearance. The absence of species identification on or directly adjacent to the landscape plan drawing violates this convention.

comment: Large trees (40+ feet mature height per ECM Appendix F) are not differentiated on landscape plan or plant schedule. Add mature height designations from ECM Appendix F to the plant schedule and identify large trees on the landscape plan with a distinct symbol or notation to allow clearance verification from overhead electric facilities.
applicableAreas: Throughout site, particularly near overhead electric line on southern boundary
observation: Sheet 35 plant schedule lists tree quantities but does not provide mature heights from ECM Appendix F for any species. The schedule shows only container specifications and planting heights (16' minimum for Live Oak and Cedar Elm containers, 8-10' minimum for ornamental trees). The landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not differentiate trees by size category, and provides no notation or legend entry indicating which trees are 'large trees' (40+ ft mature height). The vision analysis indicated that the key note legend on Sheet 31 categorizes trees by mitigation status (SY, PL, P, M) but not by size. Without mature height information on either the plant schedule or landscape plan, it is not possible to identify which proposed trees are large trees (40+ ft) requiring special clearance verification from overhead electric facilities.
reasoning: Per Reviewer Convention, large trees (40+ ft mature height per ECM Appendix F) must be differentiated on plans to allow verification that they maintain proper clearances from overhead electric facilities. The plant schedule lists species and container sizes but omits the ECM Appendix F mature heights that would define trees as 'large.' The landscape plan shows generic tree symbols without size notation. The distinction between 'large' and non-large trees is critical because large trees require 25-foot clearance from distribution conductors (vs. 15 feet for non-UC trees and 50 feet from transmission conductors). Without differentiation on the plans, reviewers cannot determine whether clearance violations exist. The status is unclear rather than fail because: (1) the information exists in the plant schedule and could be supplemented with mature height data, and (2) it is possible that none of the proposed trees are large trees, though the presence of Live Oak (likely 40+ ft) suggests otherwise.

comment: Overhead electric line shown on landscape plan but lacks dimensional clearance notation and conductor positions. Add clearance dimensions from tree trunk centers to outside conductor positions (not pole centerline) for all trees within 50 feet of overhead electric line, to verify compliance with minimum distance requirements per UCM § 1.10.10.4.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary (overhead electric line), western property boundary (overhead electric line along Valley View Road)
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows existing overhead electric (OHE) lines with two utility pole symbols: one along the western boundary (parallel to Valley View Road) and one along the southern boundary. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) also shows the OHE line as a dashed line along the southern boundary with pole symbols. However, the landscape plan does not clearly overlay or cross-reference the conductor positions from the electrical plan. The vision analysis noted that the three mitigation trees near the OHE line on Sheet 31 are shown with no dimensions or clearance notations. While the overhead line is depicted on the landscape plan, the relationship between the exact conductor locations and the proposed trees is not clearly documented. The conductor positions appear to be shown only as a schematic OHE line marking the property boundary, without indication of actual lateral offset of conductors from the pole centerline (which can be 4+ feet per the grouping guidance).
reasoning: The grouping requires that clearance verification be possible from the landscape plan. While the OHE line is shown on Sheet 31, there are no dimension lines, measurements, or notes indicating distances between the trees (especially the three trees near the southern OHE line) and the actual conductor locations. The grouping guidance specifically warns that 'measuring from pole centerline significantly underestimates actual clearance' and that 'the outermost conductor may extend 4+ feet from pole center.' Without explicit conductor positions and measured clearances, the landscape plan does not adequately document the relationship between trees and overhead facilities.

comment: Electrical transformer pads are shown on the preliminary electrical design plan near Buildings 1, 2, 4, 6, and 8, but no horizontal clearance dimensions or verification are provided demonstrating that they maintain the required 5-foot minimum distance from building foundations. Add clearance dimensions or notes on the electrical plan confirming that all transformer pads are positioned at least 5 feet from the nearest building structure.
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows five electrical transformer pads positioned on the site: west of Building 1 (northwest), southwest of Building 2 (west), east of Building 4 (center/east), east of Building 6 (east), and west of Building 8 (southwest). The transformer locations are clearly labeled with callout boxes and rectangular symbols. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows building footprints and overall site layout. However, no horizontal clearance dimensions are shown between any of the transformer pads and the building foundations or walls. The plans lack any notation, dimension line, or measurement indicating the distance from transformer pads to the nearest building structure. The Utility Notes on Sheet 21 state that "Contractor shall verify horizontal and vertical location of existing utilities prior to construction" and "notify engineer of any conflicts/discrepancies prior to installation," but this is a general directive rather than a demonstration that the 5-foot minimum clearance has been verified and documented on the plans.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires that building foundations maintain minimum 5 feet horizontal clearance from underground electric facilities (including transformer pads). The burden of demonstrating compliance is on the applicant through the site plan documentation. Presence of transformer pads on the plan combined with absence of clearance verification constitutes missing required information. The transformer locations are shown but no evidence is provided that they maintain the required 5-foot separation from buildings. Without dimension callouts, clearance arcs, or specific distance notations on the plans, it cannot be confirmed that this requirement has been addressed. The general contractor verification note is inadequate as a substitute for plan-based documentation of compliance.

comment: Retaining walls are shown on the site plan around the perimeter (north, east, and south edges) and underground electric lines are routed near these locations, but no clearance dimensions or verification are documented showing that the required 5-foot minimum separation from duct banks is maintained. Provide clearance dimensions or notes on the electrical plan confirming that all retaining wall structures are positioned at least 5 feet from underground electric facilities.
applicableAreas: Retaining walls shown along site perimeter (north, east, south boundaries)
observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) identifies multiple retaining wall segments throughout the site: a concrete retaining wall in the northeast corner along the biofiltration/detention pond, an existing retaining wall to be replaced along the entire eastern edge behind Buildings 5 and 6, and concrete retaining walls along the southern perimeter behind Buildings 7 and 8. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric lines forming a perimeter loop around the buildings, with the main lines running along the outer edges of the site where the retaining walls are located. However, no clearance dimensions are documented between the underground electric line routing and any of the retaining wall locations. No notes indicate that the required 5-foot separation has been verified. Sheet 38 (Wall Plan) would contain detailed wall dimensions and sections but was not reviewed in detail for this analysis.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires that permanent structures (including retaining walls) maintain minimum 5 feet horizontal clearance from underground electric duct banks. The site plan shows both retaining walls and electric line routing in proximity to each other, but provides no documentation that this clearance requirement has been addressed. The absence of clearance dimensions or verification notes is a deficiency—required information is missing from the plans. While the general contractor verification notes reference utility coordination, they do not substitute for plan-based documentation showing that the clearance requirement has been satisfied.

comment: Electrical pull boxes are shown on the preliminary electrical design plan in eight locations around the site perimeter, but no clearance dimensions or verification are provided demonstrating that they are located inside the property line and maintain the required 5-foot minimum distance from all sides. Add clearance dimensions or notes to the electrical plan confirming each pull box location complies with the minimum distance requirements.
applicableAreas: Electrical pull box locations distributed throughout site perimeter
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly identifies eight electrical pull box locations distributed around the site perimeter using callout boxes labeled 'Electrical Pull Box' with leader lines pointing to small nodes on the blue underground electric lines. Pull boxes are positioned: near the transformer pad west of Building 1, south of Building 2, west of Building 8, north of Building 3, east of Building 5, east of Building 6, and south of Building 7. However, the plan provides no dimension callouts, clearance arcs, or written notes indicating the horizontal distance of these pull boxes from property lines or from adjacent site features (buildings, walls, driveways, etc.). Specifically, no documentation is provided showing that pull boxes are inside the property line and maintain 5 feet clearance from all sides as required.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires that pull boxes be located inside the property line and maintain 5 feet clearance from all sides. The location of pull boxes on the plan is noted, but the specific clearance requirements are not documented. Without dimension callouts or verification notes showing that each pull box is inside the property line and maintains the required 5-foot separation, compliance cannot be confirmed. The absence of this required information on the plans constitutes a deficiency.

comment: Proposed underground electric line is shown crossing proposed water lines on the utility tap plan (Sheet 20, plan view), but no horizontal clearance dimension is documented at the crossing point. Provide a plan dimension or detail note showing that the electric conduit maintains at least 12 inches horizontal clearance from the water line at this crossing location.
applicableAreas: Water line utility tap public plan and profile crossing location
observation: Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) shows both a plan view (top portion) and a profile view (bottom portion) for the proposed water line labeled 'Wtr-Ln-A' connecting to an existing 8-inch water main. The plan view (Block 2) clearly depicts a proposed underground electric line marked with the symbol '- E -' in the legend defined as 'Proposed Underground Electric.' This electric line is drawn crossing over the water utility lines in the plan view, positioned to the east of the meter vault. However, the profile view (Block 1) does not show the electric line crossing, nor does it document any vertical clearance dimension at this crossing location. While the plan view demonstrates that the crossing occurs, there is no horizontal separation distance documented at the crossing point. The profile shows water line flowline elevations but omits the electrical facility from the profile section entirely, leaving the vertical relationship completely undocumented.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.A requires electric conduit routing to maintain minimum 12 inches (1 foot) horizontal clearance from water lines when crossing perpendicularly. The site plan documentation shows an electric line crossing water utility lines in plan view, confirming that a crossing condition exists. However, the plans provide no dimension callout or note documenting the horizontal clearance at this crossing point. The requirement is to show separation of at least 12 inches horizontally, and this required information is absent from the submitted plans. Required information is missing—specifically, the horizontal separation distance at the crossing is not documented. This is a deficiency per the standard that 'required information is absent from the plans (missing elements are deficiencies).'

comment: Proposed underground electric conduit is routed through the same utility corridors as proposed wastewater service lines, indicating crossings will occur, but no horizontal clearance dimensions are documented at the crossing locations. Provide plan dimensions or detail notes demonstrating that electric conduit maintains at least 12 inches horizontal clearance from wastewater service lines at all crossing points.
applicableAreas: Proposed wastewater service lines and internal utility routing
observation: Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) shows proposed wastewater lines (marked with 'WW' and purple/magenta coloring) routed through the central drive aisle of the property, branching to individual buildings to service the 39 units. The plan identifies a 'Duplex Grinder Pump Lift Station' in the northwest corner and '6" Cleanout' locations throughout. Sheet 20 shows the public water line profile and plan, with the proposed underground electric line ('E' symbol) visible in the plan view crossing through the same central utility corridor where wastewater lines are located. While the wastewater lines are clearly shown on Sheet 19 and the electric routing is shown on Sheet 20, no plan sheet provides documented horizontal clearance dimensions between the proposed electric conduit and the proposed wastewater service lines. The utility notes on both sheets (Blocks 16/Sheet 19 and standard Block 8/Sheet 20) contain only general contractor verification directives without specific clearance dimension documentation.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.A requires electric conduit routing to maintain minimum 12 inches (1 foot) horizontal clearance from wastewater lines when crossing perpendicularly. The site plan documents show proposed wastewater lines and proposed electric routing through the same general utility corridors and crossing areas, confirming that crossings will occur. However, no sheet provides documented horizontal clearance dimensions at these crossing points. Required information (horizontal separation distances of at least 12 inches at each crossing) is absent from the plans. This constitutes a deficiency per the standard that 'required information is absent from the plans.'

comment: Proposed water line crosses proposed underground electric line on the utility tap public plan (Sheet 20), but the vertical clearance between the facilities at the crossing point is not documented in the profile view. Add the proposed electric line to the profile view and provide a vertical clearance dimension demonstrating that the water line maintains at least 1 foot minimum vertical clearance from the underground electric facility at the crossing location.
applicableAreas: Water utility tap connection area and internal distribution
observation: Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) provides both a plan view and a profile view for the proposed water line utility connection. The plan view (Block 2) clearly shows a label '- E -' (representing Proposed Underground Electric per the legend) crossing through the utility tap area east of the meter vault, intersecting with the proposed water line routing. A notation labeled 'Proximity Call' appears on the plan view but provides no specific measurement or clearance dimension. The profile view (Block 1) shows the water line ('Wtr-Ln-A') with flowline elevations documented at key locations (FL 8" = 674.33' at the entry point, and FL 8" = 671.42' and FL Out 6" = 671.42' near the meter vault). However, the profile view does NOT show the proposed underground electric line crossing, meaning the vertical clearance between the water line and the electric line at the crossing point is completely undocumented. The 'Proximity Call' label appears to be a placeholder for coordination but contains no dimensional information.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.A requires that water lines crossing underground electric facilities maintain minimum 1 foot (12 inches) vertical clearance. The burden of demonstrating compliance is on the applicant through plan documentation. Sheet 20 plan view indicates that an electric crossing will occur (shown by the '- E -' line), and the 'Proximity Call' notation suggests the designer was aware of a proximity concern. However, the profile view—which is the correct tool for showing vertical clearance at utility crossings—completely omits the electric line from the section. No vertical clearance dimension, arc, or note documents the separation at this crossing. The applicant has failed to demonstrate compliance with the vertical clearance requirement. This is a clear deficiency: required information (vertical clearance dimensions at the water-electric crossing) is absent from the plans, and missing elements are deficiencies per the evaluation standards.

comment: Water and wastewater utilities from Austin Water are routed through the site in proximity to non-Austin Water infrastructure (electric and storm drain), but no separation distances are documented on the utility plans showing compliance with the minimum 5-foot horizontal separation requirement or the 3-foot residential service line exception. Provide dimension callouts or notes on the utility plans documenting that Austin Water infrastructure is separated from non-AW infrastructure by at least 5 feet (or 3 feet if residential service lines), as required.
applicableAreas: Utility corridors where Austin Water (water/wastewater) and non-AW infrastructure (electric, storm drain) run in proximity
observation: The site plan documents show multiple utility types routed through similar areas of the property: Sheet 19 shows water (W) and wastewater (WW) lines (Austin Water infrastructure) routed through the central drive aisles; Sheet 21 shows underground electric lines (non-AW infrastructure) forming a perimeter loop; Sheet 20 indicates an electric crossing over water facilities. The plans do not provide any dimension callouts, notes, or specifications documenting the horizontal separation distances between Austin Water infrastructure and non-AW infrastructure (particularly electric) in the utility corridors. comment: Electrical load calculations, demand projections, or capacity analysis not provided to AE Design. Submit electrical load calculations for the 39-unit development, including peak demand projections and justification for transformer sizing and service specifications shown on the site plan.

These calculations justify the service specifications and allow AE Design to verify adequacy. Absence of these calculations prevents AE Design review of electrical system adequacy.

comment: Voltage and service size specifications required for service not provided to AE Design with AE approval documentation. Provide AE Design approval letter confirming service voltage, phase configuration, and capacity specifications for the development.
observation: Sheet 21 shows preliminary electrical design with transformer and service routing but does not document voltage, phase, capacity specifications in a format submitted to AE Design. No documentation of AE Design approval for the service voltage and size specifications shown on the electrical plan.
reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires voltage and service size specifications be provided to AE Design during review. More critically, per regulatory overview, applicants cannot self-certify service specifications - AE Design must determine and approve what voltage, phases, and capacity are available and adequate at the specific location. Showing service specifications without AE Design approval documentation violates UCM § 1.3.2.

comment: Proof of correspondence with Austin Energy Design approving preliminary electric design not submitted. Provide written AE Design approval letter confirming review and approval of the preliminary electrical design plan.

reasoning: Projects requiring AE Design coordination must submit proof of correspondence with Austin Energy Design approving the preliminary electric design per UCM § 1.16.0. The completion of a completeness check does not equate to design approval. Design approval documentation is required to verify that AE Design has reviewed and approved the electric design shown on Sheet 21.

comment: Letter from Austin Energy stating utility service can be provided to site and identifying necessary easements or service upgrades not submitted. Request service verification letter from Austin Energy confirming service availability and any required easements.

This is a fundamental requirement preceding site plan approval.

comment: Agent Authorization Letter specific to Austin Energy review needs or Owner Authorization Letter explicitly stating 'Austin Energy' not provided. Submit written authorization from property owner (WM 41 Austin RE, LLC) to the agent (Bleyl Engineering) explicitly stating authority to coordinate with Austin Energy and submit electric service documentation.

A generic application signature does not satisfy this requirement for specific Austin Energy authorization.

observation: No documentation of Austin Energy Site Plan Review fee payment or submission located in supplementary documents. No receipt, fee schedule acknowledgment, or payment confirmation found.

comment: Plat notes not included as required covering: (i) Austin Energy pruning/removal rights, (ii) easement and access provision, (iii) owner erosion control and tree protection responsibilities, (iv) clearance maintenance responsibility, and (v-viii) transmission easement restrictions. Add all eight required plat notes to the site plan or create a new plat amendment with these notes.
observation: Sheet 2 displays the historical Mecey Subdivision plat recorded in 1975, which contains only the original dedication of streets and easements with no narrative plat notes. Vision analysis of the sheet confirms the absence of numbered plat notes addressing Austin Energy requirements. No plat notes found covering: (i) Austin Energy pruning/removal rights, (ii) easement and access provision, (iii) owner erosion control and tree protection responsibilities, (iv) clearance maintenance responsibility, or (v-viii) transmission easement restrictions. The project shows transmission easements and multiple utility easements per facts.md, but no accompanying plat notes documenting the requirements.

The presence of transmission lines on this site (confirmed by 16-item Electric Transmission Notes on Sheet 3) makes items (v-viii) mandatory. Complete absence of these notes is a critical deficiency.

comment: Cannot definitively verify from available evidence whether land within transmission easement is correctly excluded from parkland designation or reserved for parkland dedication. Provide explicit identification of transmission easement boundaries on landscape and plat plans with clear notation that no parkland or permanent structures are located within easement areas.
observation: Sheet 3 Electric Transmission Notes (item 16 and throughout the section) establish that transmission easements exist on the property with strict restrictions prohibiting habitable structures, storage sheds, drainage/detention ponds, and other structures that would impair AE access. Sheet 31 shows a landscape plan. Facts.md identifies transmission easement existence on the property but does not specify exact boundaries. Vision analysis of Sheet 3 confirmed the transmission easement requirements are documented but cannot visually confirm the exact spatial footprint of the transmission easement relative to proposed parkland designations on the landscape plan without additional detailed examination. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) cannot be fully evaluated for parkland designation conflicts with transmission easement location without comparative spatial analysis.
reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(9) prohibits land within transmission easements from being labeled as parkland or proposed for parkland dedication. This is a critical restriction violation if transmission easements overlap with landscape/parkland areas. The facts and Electric Transmission Notes confirm transmission easements exist; however, without access to the specific transmission easement boundary overlay and detailed landscape plan parkland designation boundaries, a definitive determination cannot be made. The requirement necessitates visual confirmation of coordinate/spatial relationships.

comment: Survey not provided showing proximities of customer's existing and/or proposed facilities to existing AE primary voltage facilities as may be required by AE Design. observation: Master Comment Report indicates Electric Review is complete and preliminary design requirements were provided. Sheet 21 shows electrical design layout but no survey demonstrating proximities of customer's existing and/or proposed facilities to existing AE primary voltage facilities. Given the presence of transmission lines and the multiple clearance requirements documented on Sheet 3, AE Design may have required such a survey. The absence of this survey prevents verification of clearance compliance.

comment: Plans show service characteristics (voltage, phases, capacity) without documentation of AE Design determination and approval. Provide AE Design approval letter confirming the service voltage, phases, and capacity shown on Sheet 21 have been determined as available and approved for the site's location and load requirements.
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) displays electrical service infrastructure with transformer pads, pull boxes, and service routing. However, no documentation is evident that the service characteristics shown (voltage, phases, capacity) have been determined and approved by AE Design. The plan appears to be applicant-prepared preliminary design rather than responsive to AE Design determinations. No AE Design approval letter confirming the service specifications are available and appropriate for the location is submitted.
reasoning: Per UCM § 1.3.2, AE Design holds exclusive determination authority for service characteristics (voltage, phases, capacity) available at any location. Applicants cannot self-certify service specifications. Plans showing service specifications without documentation of AE Design determination and approval directly violate this code section. The regulatory overview emphasizes this as a common violation pattern (violation #1).

comment: Proposed power source and service specifications (voltage, amperage, service type) not identified for proposed buildings. Specify the service voltage (primary/secondary), amperage, and service type (single/three-phase) for each building or building group on the electrical design plan.
applicableAreas: Site plan, Electrical design plan - all proposed buildings
observation: Reviewed Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) which shows 8 proposed buildings (Bldg. 1-8). Vision analysis confirms that meters are depicted on the buildings with generic 'Electrical Meters' labels, and transformers are shown as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' callouts. However, the plan does not clearly indicate the power source (service voltage, amperage, or service type) for any of the proposed buildings. The vision tool response explicitly states: 'No, projected electrical loads (kW, kVA, or amperage) are not shown anywhere on this sheet.' While the sheet shows where meters and transformers will be located graphically, there is no accompanying text, table, or note identifying the service voltage, service type (primary/secondary), or how each building will be powered.
reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) requires that plans show 'Power source for proposed buildings' as part of the application requirements for Austin Energy land development review. The grouping's Regulatory Overview states that 'Point of service identified with one service voltage' must be shown on plans (item #7 under Plan Documentation Requirements). The vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirms no text or labels indicating service voltage, amperage, or service type for the proposed buildings. While the physical locations of meters and transformers are graphically depicted, without identification of the power source (voltage level and capacity), the requirement to show 'power source for proposed buildings' is not met. This is distinct from EL-10.8 (proposed facilities shown) because the facilities themselves may be shown, but their functional designation as power source is missing.

comment: Point of service connection to existing Austin Energy infrastructure not shown on plans. Identify and label the specific connection point to the existing AE electrical system, showing the demarcation between AE-owned and customer-owned facilities.
applicableAreas: Electrical design plan - service connection point
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows the proposed electrical infrastructure on the site, including transformers, pull boxes, meters, and underground electric lines connecting buildings. Vision analysis confirms that the sheet displays 'Electrical Transformer Pad' (multiple locations near buildings), 'Underground Electric Line' routing, and 'Electrical Meters' on building exteriors. However, the plan does not show the point where the proposed electrical system connects to existing Austin Energy (AE) facilities. The vision analysis notes that 'OHE' (overhead electric) lines are shown along property boundaries as existing facilities, but there is no labeled callout or note indicating where proposed conduit or service lines connect to the existing AE infrastructure. The sheet lacks any annotation, dimension, or diagram showing the actual connection point to the existing utility lines.
reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) explicitly requires plans to show 'Point of service identified with one service voltage.' The Regulatory Overview clarifies that 'Point of service identifies the demarcation between Austin Energy-owned infrastructure and customer-owned facilities.' Without a clear point of connection shown on the plans, there is no way to determine where the demarcation occurs, which infrastructure is AE-owned vs. customer-owned, or whether the proposed service configuration complies with AE policy requiring one point of service per lot. This is a critical documentation requirement for AE review and cannot be assessed from the available plans.

comment: Proposed electrical service routing from existing Austin Energy infrastructure to proposed service not shown. Clearly show the routing path for the service entrance, including conduit sizing, length, and routing details from the point of connection to the proposed transformer locations.
observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric lines (blue solid lines with callout box labeled 'Underground Electric Line') connecting transformers and pull boxes to building meter locations. However, the vision analysis confirms that while these lines show internal site routing between proposed equipment, there is no indication of how the service enters the site or connects from the existing AE facilities at the property boundary to the proposed transformers and meters. The plan shows internal site electric routing but does not trace the service path from the point where it would connect to existing AE infrastructure (shown as 'OHE' lines and poles near property boundaries) to the proposed transformer pads and distribution points on the site.
reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) requires plans to show 'Approximate location and space for electric facilities, desired service point, projected load shown' and specifically requires documentation of 'Proposed electrical route from existing AE service to proposed service.' This requirement ensures that the applicant has coordinated with AE regarding the service entrance location, the routing path, and any required conduit or ductwork. Without this routing shown, it is unclear whether the service can physically reach the proposed transformer locations, whether it conflicts with site improvements, or whether adequate space and clearances exist. The absence of service routing from existing to proposed facilities prevents verification of the overall service design completeness.

comment: Service voltage not identified as primary or secondary. Specify on the electrical design plan whether the service is primary voltage (AE-supplied) or secondary voltage (customer-owned transformer), and label the service voltage on all applicable facilities and lines.
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical transformers, pull boxes, meters, and underground electric lines. Vision analysis of the sheet indicates that transformers are labeled generically as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' and meters are labeled as 'Electrical Meters' with no additional designation. There are no notes, labels, or callouts indicating whether the service is primary (supplied directly from AE distribution), secondary (from a customer transformer), or specifying the voltage level of the service. The overhead electric lines shown as existing ('OHE') and the proposed underground service have no voltage designations. UCM § 1.3.3 requires that service be identified as primary or secondary, and no such designation appears on the electrical design plan.
reasoning: UCM § 1.3.3 'One Point of Service and One Service Voltage' establishes that plans must identify whether the service is primary (customer receives service at AE's distribution voltage, typically 12.47kV) or secondary (customer receives service at utilization voltage, typically 120/208V or 277/480V via a customer-owned transformer). This designation is fundamental to understanding the service configuration and AE's scope of work vs. customer responsibility. Without this identification, AE cannot determine whether proposed equipment (transformers, metering) is correctly specified, whether clearances are adequate for the service voltage, and whether the service aligns with AE policy. The omission of primary vs. secondary designation prevents verification of compliance with UCM § 1.3.3.

comment: Austin Energy Standard Notes not provided on plans. Include comprehensive AE Standard Notes on the cover sheet covering easement access, tree work, clearance maintenance, and other standard Austin Energy requirements for electric service and infrastructure.
observation: Reviewed Sheet 1 (Cover Sheet) by reading the full blocks.md content for all administrative, boilerplate, and notes sections. The cover sheet contains extensive notes including: fire department requirements (Block 7), recycling ordinance (Block 15), drainage maintenance (Block 14), Edwards Aquifer note (Block 22), and other utility/environmental notes. General electrical notes appear on Sheet 3 (Block 8: 'Electric Notes' with 5 items regarding Austin Energy tree work and easements, and Block 14 with similar content, and Block 20 with 16 Electric Transmission Notes). However, the Cover Sheet (Sheet 1) contains no section titled 'AE Standard Notes' or 'Austin Energy Standard Notes.' The electrical transmission notes on Sheet 3 are present but do not constitute the standard AE Standard Notes required for all site plans. These notes address transmission line work and safety but are not comprehensive standard notes covering electric service design, clearances, easements, plat requirements, and other standard AE documentation requirements.
reasoning: The grouping's Regulatory Overview (line 40) explicitly states: 'Required Plat Notes (UCM § 1.16.0(8)): When plats are recorded as part of land development approval, specific Austin Energy notes must appear on the plat.' While plat notes are specifically for recorded plats, the checklist item EL-10.19 cites 'Reviewer Convention' which establishes that AE Standard Notes should be present on all site plans to provide standard language regarding Austin Energy's rights, owner responsibilities, and required practices. The cover sheet is the standard location for such notes. The presence of general electrical transmission notes on Sheet 3 does not satisfy the requirement for comprehensive AE Standard Notes covering all aspects of electric service design, easement management, and utility coordination.

comment: Note missing stating all electric infrastructure shown and exceptions require AE pre-approval. Add a note to the electrical design plan stating: 'All existing and proposed electric infrastructure required for service to this project is shown on this plan, except where noted separately or subject to Austin Energy Design approval.'
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) is reviewed for the presence of a note stating that all electric infrastructure (existing and proposed) is shown on the plan or noting exceptions requiring AE pre-approval. The vision analysis of Sheet 21 explicitly confirms: 'No, there is no note at the top or anywhere else on the sheet with that specific phrasing or similar language indicating completeness of the electric infrastructure shown.' The sheet contains general utility notes (Block 6 on the blocks.md states 'Contractor shall verify horizontal and vertical location of existing utilities' and disclaimers about existing utility locations). However, there is no affirmative statement indicating that all existing and proposed electric infrastructure requiring approval has been shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan, nor any notation of exceptions that require separate AE approval.
reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires that plans show 'All existing electric facilities (transmission/distribution structures, guys, anchors, transformers)' and 'All existing and proposed permanent structures' and 'Sufficient clearances demonstrated for existing and proposed electric facilities.' Without a note stating that all infrastructure is shown (or exceptions noted), reviewers cannot determine whether missing elements are intentional omissions subject to later AE approval or unintentional oversights. The Regulatory Overview section lists common violation patterns: 'Missing plat note requirements' and identifies that the grouping addresses 'what must be shown on plans to demonstrate a complete electric design.' A note confirming completeness or documenting exceptions is essential to that completeness demonstration. The title 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' suggests the design is not yet final, but even preliminary submissions must include a note about completeness or noted exceptions.

comment: Electrical easements not distinguished as aerial vs. underground. Label all electrical easements to specify whether they accommodate aerial facilities (overhead poles, conductors, guy wires) or underground facilities (conduits, pad-mounted equipment, buried laterals), and ensure clearance requirements are applied appropriately to each type.
applicableAreas: Plans showing electrical easements - Site Plan (Sheet 9), Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), Plat (Sheet 2), Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), Grading Plan (Sheet 11)
observation: Examined Sheet 2 (Plat) vision analysis: Easements are shown with width dimensions (5' P.U.E., 5' Elec. & Tel. Easement, 5' Elec. Easement) but the vision analysis explicitly states: 'No. The labels on the plat do not contain the words "aerial," "overhead," or "underground."' Sheet 21 vision analysis confirms: 'Existing easements are shown (as noted above). However, the labels do not explicitly distinguish between "aerial" or "underground" within the easement text itself (they are generally labeled "P.U.E." or "Elec. & Tele. Easement"). The lines running through or near some of these easements are labeled "OHE" (Overhead Electric), implying aerial use in those specific areas, but the easement labels themselves do not make this distinction.' Sheet 9 vision analysis notes: '5' Electric Easement is labeled along the right (eastern) property boundary' and '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement labeled near the bottom right' but no distinction of type. Both aerial (overhead conductors, poles, service drops, guy wires) and underground (conduit, pad-mounted transformers) electric infrastructure exist on this site. The regulatory overview explicitly distinguishes these: 'Aerial electric easements accommodate overhead facilities... with vertical sky-to-ground clearance requirements; non-aerial easements accommodate underground facilities... with horizontal and subsurface clearance requirements.' Without this distinction labeled on easements, plan reviewers cannot verify that clearances and access are adequate for the actual facility type using each easement.
reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires plans to show 'All public and private easements (electrical, gas, water, sewer, telecommunications, drainage) with locations and extents clearly delineated.' The grouping's Code References section (lines 72-90) identifies UCM § 1.10.3 and § 1.10.4 as establishing different clearance requirements for aerial vs. non-aerial easements. The Regulatory Overview specifically states: 'Plans must distinguish between: Aerial vs. Non-Aerial Easements: Aerial electric easements accommodate overhead facilities (poles, overhead conductors, service drops, guy wires) with vertical sky-to-ground clearance requirements (7.5 ft horizontal, 15-ft radius); non-aerial easements accommodate underground facilities (conduit, pad-mounted transformers, underground laterals).' Without this distinction labeled on the plans themselves, it is impossible to verify that clearances meet requirements for the type of facility in each easement. Both overhead and underground facilities are shown on this site (OHE lines on Sheet 21, underground conduits on Sheet 21), confirming that both easement types exist.

comment: Recording information (volume/page, document number, or plat reference) not provided for existing electrical easements. Add recording information to all easement labels, cross-referencing the Travis County plat or deed document where the easement was recorded (e.g., 'Vol. 73, Pg. 76, Case C8S-75-160').
applicableAreas: All sheets showing electrical easements - Plat (Sheet 2), Site Plan (Sheet 9), Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), and others
observation: Sheet 2 (Plat) vision analysis explicitly confirms: 'No. While there are volume and page references shown on the plat (in circles indicating adjacent property deed records, e.g., Vol. 3058 Pg. 2327), there are no specific Volume/Page references or document numbers attached directly to the easement labels themselves. The labels only indicate if they are "(Exist.)" or "(Existing)."' Sheet 21 vision analysis confirms easements are shown with labels like '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 385 D.R.T.C.Tx.' (which does have recording info on this sheet), but upon closer examination, sheet 9 shows '5' Electric Easement' and '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement' with no volume/page references shown. The facts.md document (lines 135-143) identifies several existing electric easements: '5' Electric Easements (×2)' with 'Document Ref: Travis County Doc 73/76, Case C8S-75-160' and '7.5' Public Utility Easement' with the same reference. These recorded documents should be cited on the plans. On Sheet 2, the plat does not include volume/page references for the electric easement labels, representing an omission of required recording information.
reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires easements to be shown 'with locations and extents clearly delineated.' The term 'clearly delineated' encompasses not only spatial location and width but also legal identification. The Regulatory Overview explicitly states: 'Recording information: Electric infrastructure documentation requirements... UCM § 1.16.0 serves as the comprehensive baseline for land development review applications, specifying what must be shown on plans to obtain Austin Energy approval.' LDC § 25-4-132 (cited in Code References) requires 'Easement dimensions, locations, and designations to match exactly between plat and site plan.' Without recording information (volume/page or document number), easement locations cannot be verified against recorded documents, overlapping or conflicting easements cannot be identified, and the legal identity of each easement is unclear. This is particularly important where multiple easements may exist on the same site (this site has at least 7-9 documented easements per facts.md). Recording information must appear on all plan sheets showing easements.

comment: Electric facilities not shown consistently across all required plan sheets. Show all proposed electric facilities (transformers, pull boxes, meters, underground conduit routing, easements) on Site Plan (Sheet 9), Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), and Grading Plan (Sheet 11) with consistent symbols and locations matching Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan).
applicableAreas: Site Plan (Sheet 9), Utility Plan (Sheet 21), Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), Grading Plan (Sheet 11)
observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) vision analysis confirms: 'Transformer Pad (Typ.) is explicitly shown and labeled on the west side... Individual meters, pull boxes, and detailed underground electrical conduits routing to the specific buildings are not visibly drawn or labeled on this sheet.' Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows comprehensive electrical facilities (transformers, pull boxes, meters, underground lines) with explicit labels. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) vision analysis states: 'There are no clear labels or specific symbols explicitly identifying electrical facilities such as transformers, meters, or pull boxes on this landscape plan sheet.' Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) guide mentions 'utility easements' but vision analysis reveals electrical infrastructure details are not shown there. The grouping's Documents to Review section (lines 94-103) specifies: 'Verify all electric facilities and easements shown consistently across sheets' and lists 'Site Plan, Utility Plan, Landscape Plan, Grading Plan, Irrigation Plan' as required sheets. Detailed electrical facilities shown on Sheet 21 are not shown consistently on all other sheets where they should appear (particularly Landscape and Grading plans where transformer locations and clearances are critical).
reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires plans to show electric infrastructure, and the grouping's common violation patterns specifically identify: 'Cross-sheet inconsistency: Electric facilities shown on utility plan but omitted from landscape, grading, or irrigation plans where coordination is critical (especially down guy anchors conflicting with accessible paths, trees conflicting with clearance envelopes).' The principle is that all infrastructure must be consistently shown on all sheets where coordination is necessary. The Regulatory Overview states (line 54): 'Cross-sheet inconsistency: Electric facilities shown on utility plan but omitted from landscape, grading, or irrigation plans where coordination is critical.' This project shows detailed electrical design on Sheet 21 but lacks consistent electrical facility depiction on Landscape (Sheet 31) and Grading (Sheet 11) plans, preventing verification of clearances, coordination with other site features, and staging area adequacy.

comment: Tree locations not coordinated with overhead electric line clearances. Relocate all landscape plantings (particularly trees with mature canopies) to maintain minimum 15-foot radial clearance from the overhead electric (OHE) lines shown along the southern property boundary.
applicableAreas: Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) - southern property boundary where overhead electric lines run
observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows overhead electric lines labeled 'OHE' running horizontally along the bottom (southern) edge of the site. Vision analysis explicitly confirms: 'Yes, overhead electric lines are shown. A line clearly labeled "---OHE---" runs horizontally along the bottom edge of the site plan. Regarding vegetation clearance, there does NOT appear to be clear clearance. Several proposed tree symbols (circles representing canopies) are drawn directly overlapping or immediately adjacent to the "OHE" line, particularly towards the bottom right section of the plan.' The Regulatory Overview (lines 61-64) establishes clearance requirements: 'Distribution facilities (<60kV, typically 12.47kV) with 15-foot radial clearances' and more specifically 'Permanent clearances from overhead distribution (UCM § 1.10.3): 7.5 feet minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead primary, neutral, secondary conductors; 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors.' Trees directly adjacent to overhead lines violate this 15-foot radial clearance requirement.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires '15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors.' This is a safety clearance to prevent tree branches and fall hazards from contacting energized conductors. The grouping's Common Violation Patterns section (line 54) specifically identifies: 'trees conflicting with clearance envelopes' as a cross-sheet coordination problem. Vision analysis of Sheet 31 confirms trees are 'directly overlapping or immediately adjacent to the OHE line' rather than maintaining 15-foot separation. This represents a direct conflict between the landscape design (trees) and the electrical infrastructure (OHE lines with required 15-foot clearance). Sheet 21 shows the overhead electric lines exist on this site, and Sheet 31 landscape plan fails to maintain required clearance from those existing lines.

comment: Projected electrical load not shown on plans. Calculate and show the total electrical load for the project (in kW or kVA) and identify the load for each building or service point, based on building size, occupancy classification, and code-required minimum loads.
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) is reviewed for the presence of projected electrical load information. Vision analysis explicitly confirms: 'No, projected electrical loads (kW, kVA, or amperage) are not shown anywhere on this sheet.' The sheet contains building square footage and finished floor elevations (e.g., 'Bldg. 1: 3,290 sf, FFE = 687.50'), but there is no statement of total project electrical load, load per building, service amperage, or any other load specification. The sheet title block designates it as 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' but contains no load calculations or specifications.
reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) explicitly requires that plans show 'Projected electrical load required for electric service' as part of the application requirements. The Regulatory Overview (lines 32-33) states that the plan documentation must show 'Approximate location and space for electric facilities, desired service point, projected load shown' as item #8 in the comprehensive baseline for applications. Projected load is essential information for Austin Energy to determine service requirements, transformer sizing, and capacity. Without projected load, AE cannot verify that the proposed transformer(s) are adequately sized, that conduit sizing is appropriate, or that the overall service design meets load demands.

comment: No clearance verification exhibits provided demonstrating compliance with both the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radius cylindrical clearance requirements from overhead distribution conductors as required by AEDC § 1.10.3. Engineered and sealed clearance exhibits must be included in the permitted plan set.
applicableAreas: Site-wide clearance zones around existing electric facilities
observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) and Sheet 9 (Site Plan) to determine if clearance verification exhibits are provided. Sheet 21 shows underground electric lines, transformers, pull boxes, and meters with building footprints and FFEs labeled. Sheet 9 shows electric facility locations with property lines and easement boundaries. No dedicated clearance verification exhibits found on any sheet examined. No sheet displays both required clearance envelopes: the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance extending infinitely upward from 7.5 feet horizontal distance from conductors, AND the 15-foot radius cylindrical clearance extending infinitely downward from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. No engineered and sealed clearance exhibit sheets appear in the 39-sheet plan set.
reasoning: The checklist item requires clearance verification exhibits to be 'engineered and scaled' and 'included in the permitted plan set' when proposed structures are located within required clearance zones. AEDC § 1.16.0(2) mandates this documentation. While the electrical design plan shows proposed structures and electric facility locations, it does not provide a dedicated exhibit demonstrating compliance with both the 7'-6" horizontal AND 15-foot radius clearance requirements. The absence of clearance verification exhibits means the applicant cannot demonstrate code compliance with these dual clearance envelopes, which the grouping Regulatory Overview specifies must BOTH be satisfied simultaneously—satisfying one does not satisfy the other.

comment: Profile or cross-section drawings not provided demonstrating clearances between proposed building elements (including overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) and existing electric facilities. Engineered profiles drawn to scale and sealed must show vertical clearances and building element dimensions.
applicableAreas: All building elevations where overhangs, balconies, awnings, or canopies exist
observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) for profile/cross-section drawings showing clearances. Found only plan view with building footprints and FFEs; no profiles shown on this sheet. Examined Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) which contains detailed water utility profiles at 1"=20' horizontal and 1"=2' vertical scale. However, these profiles show ONLY water utility lines and do not include electric utility lines or building elements (walls, overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) needed to verify clearances from existing electric facilities. No building elevation sheets provided in the plan set that would show heights and element dimensions of proposed structures.
