Metering method (CT metered at the transformer vs. building metered) affects meter placement, conductor sizing, and point-of-service configuration. For multi-unit developments, UCM § 1.9.3.4 requires that when two or more meters are served from one service connection, meters and disconnects must be grouped in a common location (meter bank/SDE) with specified clearances and line-of-sight requirements. Omitting metering method prevents verification of compliance with grouping and accessibility standards.

comment: Transformers not delineated in legend as proposed utilities. Add a Utility Legend to the site plan, wet utilities plan, and electrical plan defining the symbols for: (1) Transformer Pad, (2) Proposed Underground Electric Line, (3) Electrical Meter, (4) Electrical Easement, and (5) Pull Box. Use consistent symbols across all sheets. Ensure symbols are actually applied on the plans.
observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) contains no utility legend. Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) contains no utility legend defining transformer or meter symbols. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) contains a Legend in the top-right corner that defines two electrical symbols: "- E - Proposed Underground Electric" and "[Square symbol] Transformer Pad". However, on Sheet 19, neither of these symbols are actually drawn on the plan—the legend defines symbols that are not used. Sheets 11, 12, and 31 contain no transformer symbols or legends.
reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires plans to delineate proposed utilities clearly. A utility legend is the standard method for communicating utility symbols and line types. The absence of a consistent legend across the site plan set, combined with the fact that the legend on Sheet 19 defines symbols that are not actually used, violates the clarity requirement. Austin Energy and City reviewers expect a unified legend identifying all proposed electrical infrastructure (transformers, meters, underground lines, easements) with symbols consistently applied across all relevant sheets.

comment: Meter locations not shown on all required plan sheets. Show all electrical meter locations on the site plan, wet utilities plan, and landscape plan. Identify each meter location with a callout and label. Note whether meters are grouped (per UCM § 1.9.3.4) or individual. Verify that each meter location is: (1) at ground level, (2) readily accessible, (3) within sight of its serving transformer, and (4) positioned with disconnects within 20 feet for grouped configurations.
observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows 8 meter locations labeled "Electrical Meters" on building exterior walls. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows one gas meter but does not show electrical meter locations. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) has a legend entry for utility symbols but no meters are drawn on the plan. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does not show electrical meter locations. The required site plan, wet utilities plan, and landscape plan all lack electrical meter documentation.
reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1.A requires meter locations to be shown on plans. Meters must be on first floor or ground level, readily accessible, within sight of the transformer, and for grouped metering, positioned with disconnects in a common location per UCM § 1.9.3.4. The absence of meter locations on the site plan and landscape plan prevents verification of accessibility, sightlines to transformers, and clearances from other utilities. For a multi-unit development, meter locations are essential to demonstrating that the metering and disconnection configuration complies with grouped metering requirements.

comment: Meters and disconnects not labeled on all required sheets. Label all electrical meters and disconnects on the site plan, wet utilities plan, and landscape plan. For grouped metering, label the service distribution enclosure (SDE) and wireway location, and note the distance between meters and disconnects (maximum 20 feet, must be within line of sight per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J). Specify meter specifications (single-phase, three-phase, main vs. sub-meter).
observation: Sheet 21 labels meters as "Electrical Meters" with callout lines to building wall locations. Sheets 9, 19, and 31 do not show meters or meter labels. No callouts define meter specifications, disconnect locations, service distribution enclosure locations, or grouping configurations. For a multi-unit residential development, disconnect locations are not identified relative to meters.
reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 and § 1.16.0 require that plans clearly identify meter and disconnect locations. Meter labels and disconnect callouts enable Austin Energy to verify that the service configuration is accessible, properly grouped (if applicable), and compliant with spacing requirements (maximum 20 feet between meter and disconnect per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J). Without labels and callouts on the site, wet utilities, and landscape plans, the reviewer cannot confirm that the metering design meets code requirements across all plan disciplines.

comment: Meter sight line to transformer not verified. Show on the electrical plan or a separate diagram that each electrical meter is within clear sight line of its serving transformer. If any meter does not have direct line of sight to the nearest transformer, provide written approval from Austin Energy Design and Distribution Metering business units for the exception. Provide sight line diagrams or cross-reference elevation views confirming visibility.
observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meter locations on building exterior walls and 4 transformer pad locations distributed across the site. Meters appear to be positioned on various building sides (north, west, south, east). Transformers are located in northwest, southwest, northeast, and southeast areas. Without clear sight line diagrams, elevation views, or explicit distance callouts, it is not possible to verify that all 8 meters are within sight of an Austin Energy transformer. The term "within sight" in UCM § 1.9.3.1.B does not specify a distance limit (older references to "150 ft line of sight" are not codified), but direct visual contact must be apparent. Given the distributed meter and transformer locations, several meters may not have clear line-of-sight to a transformer.
reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1.B requires meters to be within sight of an Austin Energy transformer. The grouping notes that "within sight" visibility is the current code requirement with no maximum distance specified, but direct visual contact is required. Without sight line diagrams showing clear, unobstructed lines between each meter and its serving transformer, the reviewer cannot confirm compliance. The scattered distribution of transformers and meters across 8 buildings suggests that some meters may be obstructed by building walls or other structures, requiring line-of-sight verification or AE Design approval for exceptions.

comment: Point-of-service location not shown. Identify and label the point-of-service (POS) location(s) where Austin Energy conductors connect to customer conductors. This may be at a meter socket, pedestal, SDE (service distribution enclosure), pull box, or other approved enclosure. Label with "Point of Service" notation and specify the type of enclosure. Verify that all customer conductors originate from the labeled POS.
observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electrical routing, transformer pads, and meter locations, but does not explicitly identify or label a point-of-service (POS) location. UCM § 1.3.4 defines point of service as the location where Austin Energy's conductors connect with the customer's conductors. The plan shows meters on building walls and transformers in common areas but does not label the specific location(s) where the connection point(s) between AE and customer infrastructure occur. No callout identifies the meter socket, pedestal, service distribution enclosure, pull box, or other location where the POS connection is made.
reasoning: UCM § 1.3.4 defines point of service as a critical infrastructure element. The POS location must be clearly identified because it designates the boundary between Austin Energy responsibility (up to the POS) and customer responsibility (from the POS onward). Without explicit POS identification, the reviewer cannot verify that the service configuration is properly documented, that customer conductors are correctly routed, and that Austin Energy access to the service point is protected. For multi-unit developments, the POS is especially important for understanding service distribution, metering grouping, and disconnect coordination.

comment: Service conductors from point of service to AE facilities not clearly identified. Label the point where the underground service stub enters the site and the point of service connection (where AE and customer conductors meet). Show the routing clearly with callouts identifying: (1) service entry point from AE (duct bank, pole, or underground source), (2) point of service location, (3) service distribution enclosure (SDE) or main disconnect location, (4) direction of conductor flow to transformers and meter banks. Verify that service conductors are protected per code and sized per load calculations.
observation: Sheet 21 shows "Underground Electric Line" routing from the west property edge, through pull boxes, to transformers and meter locations. The underground line enters the site from the left (west) boundary and is drawn as a continuous blue line. However, the plan does not explicitly label: (1) where the service stub originates or enters the site, (2) the specific point of service where AE and customer conductors connect, (3) the direction of conductor flow from the POS to transformers and meters. The routing is shown but the origin point and termination points are not clearly called out.
reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that service conductor routing be clearly shown from point of service to AE facilities (transformer). The current documentation shows the routing line but lacks explicit identification of the POS location and the service stub entry point. This creates ambiguity: it is unclear whether the line entering from the west represents a service drop from overhead AE lines, an underground service stub from an AE duct bank, or another configuration. Without explicit callouts identifying the POS and service origin, Austin Energy cannot confirm that customer conductors are properly sized, protected, and routed.

comment: Proposed trees on the western property boundary are positioned directly on or within 5 lateral feet of the underground electric line. Remove trees from this zone or relocate the underground electric line to achieve minimum 5-foot clearance.
applicableAreas: Western property boundary street yard area
observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) at 1"=20' scale shows proposed trees (marked with 'M' and 'ST' symbols indicating mitigation and street yard trees) positioned directly overlapping or immediately adjacent to the underground electric line marked '-E-' running along the western property boundary. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) confirms underground electric lines route along this boundary. The vision analysis explicitly stated: 'Several tree symbols (tagged 'M' and 'ST') are drawn physically overlapping or immediately adjacent to the '-E-' line. Based on the 1"=20' scale, these proposed trees appear to be placed directly on top of, or within 5 feet of, this underground line.' This indicates violation of the 0-5 foot no-tree zone required for underground electric equipment.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits any trees within 5 lateral feet of underground electric equipment (conduits, duct banks, cables, vaults, manholes, transformers). The landscape plan shows trees positioned directly over or immediately adjacent to the documented underground electric line. The visual positioning demonstrated in the plan drawings indicates non-compliance with the absolute 5-foot clearance requirement. This is not a case of approximate positioning that could be verified in the field—the plan itself shows the violation.

comment: Provide root barrier construction details (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment edge) for all trees planted within 5-20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment. Include typical cross-sections on detail sheets and cross-reference on landscape plan.
applicableAreas: Areas where trees are proposed within 5-20 feet of underground electric equipment
observation: Sheet 31 shows proposed trees and shrubs throughout the site near underground electric infrastructure. Sheet 37 (Landscape Details) provides standard tree planting details (Standard 610S-4 protection detail, tree planting pit specifications) but contains no root barrier construction details meeting UCM § 1.10.10.4 requirements (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned exactly 5 feet from equipment edge). The plant list on Sheet 35 identifies 12 trees being planted throughout the property near electric facilities, but no detail sheets show root barrier specifications coordinated with underground electric locations. The only root-related details on Sheet 37 describe tree protection during construction and standard planting practices, not UCM-compliant root barriers for electrical equipment protection.
reasoning: For trees planted between 5-20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment, UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires root barriers minimum 4 feet deep, positioned exactly 5 feet from the equipment edge. The landscape documentation does not provide these specific root barrier details for any trees positioned in this clearance zone. Standard tree planting details do not satisfy the specialized root barrier requirement for proximity to electrical infrastructure. The lack of any reference to UCM root barrier specifications in the landscape notes or details indicates non-compliance.

comment: Overlay transformer pad locations (from Sheet 21) on the landscape plan (Sheet 31) and show 10-foot clearance zone around each pad. Verify all proposed trees and shrubs are outside these zones, or obtain Austin Energy written approval for any trees within this clearance.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations throughout site (5 pads identified on Sheet 21)
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows 5 transformer pads positioned at specific locations: adjacent to Bldg. 1 (near entrance), adjacent to Bldg. 2, in courtyard between Bldgs. 4/5, in courtyard between Bldgs. 6/7, and adjacent to Bldg. 8. However, Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does not show these transformer pad locations or their 10-foot clearance zones. The landscape plan shows multiple proposed trees throughout the site without reference to transformer locations, making it impossible to verify that trees are kept outside the 10-foot minimum clearance zone required by UCM § 1.10.10.4.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits trees within 10 lateral feet of pad-mounted transformers or electric equipment. The applicant must demonstrate compliance by showing transformer locations and clearance zones on the landscape plan. The absence of transformer pads on the landscape plan means the applicant has not provided the minimum required documentation to verify compliance. This is a coordination failure between electrical design and landscape design.

comment: Show transmission easement boundaries on the landscape plan. Verify and document that no proposed trees or shrubs are located within transmission easement areas. If any trees currently exist within transmission easements, indicate their removal or obtain Austin Energy written approval.
observation: The property plat (Sheet 2) and facts.md document record that electric easements exist on the property, including plat-dedicated 5-foot electric easements. Sheet 3 (General Notes, Block 20) explicitly states: 'No trees shall be planted within the transmission easement. No trees shall be planted within 25 feet of the base of the transmission structure.' However, the landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not show transmission easement boundaries, preventing verification that no trees are planted within transmission easements. Without visible easement boundaries overlaid on the landscape plan, compliance with the absolute prohibition on trees within transmission easements cannot be verified.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits all trees from being planted within electric transmission easements (facilities ≥60kV phase-to-phase). This is an absolute requirement with no exceptions based on tree size or species. The site plan notes on Sheet 3 reiterate this requirement. The applicant must show transmission easement boundaries on the landscape plan and demonstrate that no trees are positioned within them. The absence of easement boundaries on the landscape plan constitutes non-compliance with the documentation requirement.

comment: Obtain a License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement before installing any landscaping, trees, irrigation, or plantings within electric easement areas. Provide executed copy with final site plan submittal or reference execution in a plan note.
observation: Review of all available site plan documents and supplementary documents (including Master Comment Report) reveals no executed license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement for landscaping, trees, or irrigation within electric easement areas. The Master Comment Report (Electric Review section) references Austin Energy preliminary design requirements including UCM § 1.10.10.3, which requires a License Agreement before installing landscaping in electric easement areas. No such agreement is attached to the plans, referenced in any plan notes, or mentioned in any accompanying documentation. Sheet 31 shows trees proposed in areas where electric easements exist (per property records), but there is no evidence of the required license agreement.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 explicitly requires that 'a License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement is required before installing landscaping, trees, irrigation, or plantings that might obstruct access to Austin Energy facilities within electric easement areas. The agreement must be obtained and filed before the activity occurs.' The absence of this license agreement documentation on or with the site plan is a deficiency. While license agreements are administrative documents that may be obtained after plan approval, the applicant must provide evidence that the requirement has been addressed (or provide the executed agreement).

comment: Identify and show utility pole locations from Sheet 21 on the landscape plan. Mark 10-foot clearance zones around each pole and verify all proposed trees are outside these zones.
applicableAreas: Utility pole locations along street right-of-way
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows utility poles depicted as small circles with crosshairs located along the far left edge of the property along the street right-of-way. The landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not show these utility pole locations. Without the pole locations shown on the landscape plan, there is no means to verify that proposed trees maintain the required 10-foot minimum clearance from poles.

The absence of pole locations on the landscape plan means the applicant has not provided sufficient documentation to verify this clearance requirement.

comment: Show transformer pad locations and access door orientations on the landscape plan. Mark 10-foot clearance zones on access door sides and verify no shrubs are positioned within these zones.
observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads with their locations but does not clearly indicate access door orientations. Sheet 31 shows shrubs and low vegetation symbols throughout the site (marked PM=Dwarf Palmetto, MB=Big Muhly, GC=Gulf Muhly, LS=Texas Sage, MC=Dwarf Wax Myrtle per Sheet 35) but does not show transformer pad locations or access door sides to verify 10-foot clearance.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 specifies that no shrubs be planted within 10 lateral feet of the access door side (hot-stick-use area/pad-locked side) of pad-mounted equipment. Without transformer locations and their access door orientations shown on the landscape plan, the applicant cannot demonstrate compliance.

comment: Show transformer pad locations and identify access vs. non-access sides on the landscape plan. Verify shrubs are at least 5 feet from non-access sides.
observation: Same as EL-16.15: transformer pad locations and orientations not shown on landscape plan, preventing verification of 5-foot shrub clearance on non-access sides.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires minimum 5-foot clearance from non-access sides of pad-mounted equipment. Landscape plan must show transformer locations and orientations to verify this clearance.

comment: Show vault and manhole locations from Sheet 21 on the landscape plan. Mark 8-foot clearance zones around each vault/manhole requiring personnel access and verify shrubs and obstructions are outside these zones.
applicableAreas: Subsurface electric vaults and manhole locations
observation: Sheet 21 shows vault and manhole locations (including a labeled 'Vault Easement' at transformer pad near Bldg. 8). Sheet 31 does not show these vault/manhole locations. Without them overlaid on the landscape plan, the required 8-foot clearance zone around vaults/manholes cannot be verified.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 requires minimum 8-foot clearance around all pedestals, subsurface vaults, or manholes requiring personnel access. The landscape plan must show vault/manhole locations to enable verification.

comment: Show transformer locations and identify access doors on the landscape plan. Verify that no trees block the route from each transformer access door to the nearest drivable surface (street, alley, or parking area).
applicableAreas: Space between transformer access doors and drivable surfaces
observation: Transformer pad locations not shown on landscape plan, preventing verification of tree-free access routes from transformer access doors to drivable surfaces (streets, alleys, parking areas).
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits trees between the access door of pad-mounted equipment and drivable surfaces used for truck access. This zone must remain clear for bucket truck positioning during hot-stick work. Verification requires transformer locations and access routes to be shown on the landscape plan.

comment: Show transformer locations and required truck access routes on the landscape plan. Verify no trees block access lanes or turning radii required for Austin Energy service vehicles (typical 40-50 ft turning radius for bucket trucks).
applicableAreas: Transformer locations and access routes throughout site
observation: Transformer pad locations from Sheet 21 and access routes from Sheet 9 (Site Plan) are not overlaid on the landscape plan (Sheet 31). Without this coordination, it cannot be verified that proposed trees do not obstruct access routes or turning radii for bucket trucks used to service transformers and Austin Energy equipment.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 states that landscaping must not restrict Austin Energy personnel and equipment access. The landscape plan must show transformer locations and access requirements to demonstrate compliance. The absence of this coordination indicates non-compliance with the access requirement.

comment: Show vault locations on the landscape plan with tree locations and estimated mature canopy spreads. Verify no trees are positioned to create overhead obstruction of vault covers/lids.
observation: Vault locations shown on Sheet 21 are not shown on landscape plan (Sheet 31). Vault covers/lids must remain clear of tree canopy for operational access, but without vault locations on the landscape plan, this cannot be verified.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 requires that vaults remain accessible for personnel and equipment. Trees positioned over vault covers prevent access operations. The landscape plan must show vault locations and tree canopy spreads to verify compliance.

comment: Overlay all electric facilities from Sheet 21 onto the landscape plan (Sheet 31), including transformer pads, underground electric lines (with 5-foot and broader clearance zones clearly marked), pull boxes, utility poles, vault locations, electric easement boundaries, and transmission easement boundaries. This overlay is essential for verifying compliance with all vegetation clearance requirements.
applicableAreas: Entire site - all utility and landscape areas
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows all electric facilities: transformer pads, underground electric lines (marked '-E-'), pull boxes, meter banks, utility poles, vault easement, and various utility easements. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does not show any of these electric facilities. The landscape plan shows only landscape elements (trees, shrubs, paving, contours, irrigation notes) without any reference to electrical infrastructure locations. This prevents all clearance verifications required by checklist items EL-16.1 through EL-16.21.
reasoning: Proper coordination between electrical and landscape design requires that electric facilities be shown on the landscape plan at the same scale. This allows visual verification of clearance zones, easement boundaries, and access routes. The absence of electrical infrastructure on the landscape plan is a fundamental coordination failure that prevents the reviewer from verifying compliance with any of the electric facility proximity requirements. This is not optional—it is a standard requirement for site plan review.

comment: Point of electric service (POS) location is not explicitly designated on required plan sheets. Add clear labeling of the point of service location (meter socket, pedestal, pull-box, or AE-designated enclosure) on all required sheets per UCM § 1.16.0(6) and UCM § 1.4.2.6.
observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan), Sheet 9 (Site Plan), and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan). Sheet 21 shows underground electric routing originating from west side of property but no specific label for "Point of Service" or "POS"; the connection point is shown but not explicitly designated as the POS per AE Design requirements. Sheet 9 shows a single transformer pad but no POS designation. Sheet 31 shows only overhead electric line on boundary, no POS marked. The point of service location and primary source location are not clearly labeled or designated on any of the required plan sheets.
reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires the point of electric service to be shown on plan sheets per UCM § 1.4.2.6 requirements. While Sheet 21 shows electrical infrastructure and apparent connection points, these are not explicitly labeled as the "Point of Service" or identified as the location where Austin Energy's and the customer's conductors connect. Per UCM § 1.3.4, the POS is the specific location of connection or termination. The absence of explicit POS designation on required sheets (Site Plan and Landscape Plan) means the POS location cannot be verified as shown per code requirements. On Sheet 21, while the general routing is shown, the specific POS is not called out.

comment: Underground electric conduit routing and service lines must be shown on all required plan sheets including site plan showing all utilities (Sheet 9) and landscape plan (Sheet 31). Add underground electric line routing showing connections from property line source through site to service connection points per UCM § 1.4.2.6.
observation: Sheet 21 shows complete underground electric line routing from street entry point through site with conduit paths and connection to pull boxes and meters. Sheet 9 (Site Plan showing all utilities) shows water (-W-), sanitary sewer (-WW-), and storm drain (-SD-) routing, but does NOT show underground electric line routing despite electric infrastructure being shown elsewhere on the site plan (one transformer pad noted). Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows only overhead electric (OHE) on the boundary, with no underground conduit or cable routing depicted. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) includes electrical symbols in the legend (-E- for Proposed Underground Electric) but contains NO actual underground electric lines drawn on the plan.
reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires underground electric cabling routing and service lines to be shown on required plan sheets including site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and all electrical plans. The inconsistency across sheets violates this requirement. While detailed electrical routing is shown on the dedicated Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), the required plan sheets per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B (Site Plan and Landscape Plan) do not show this infrastructure. The absence of underground electric routing on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) is particularly significant, as this sheet shows other underground utilities (water, sewer, storm) in detail but omits electrical routing. Similarly, the Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19) shows a legend entry for proposed underground electric but draws no such lines, creating an incomplete utility coordination drawing.

comment: Transformer pad locations must be shown on the landscape plan (Sheet 31) and site plan showing all utilities (Sheet 9). Show all transformer pad locations with corresponding labels to ensure proper coordination with landscape design and site layout per UCM § 1.4.2.6.
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows 5 transformer pads with specific locations labeled (near northwest entrance, west of Bldg 2, east of Bldg 4, west of Bldg 8, east of Bldg 7). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows one transformer pad labeled as "Transformer Pad (Typ.)" on the west side near Building 1. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does NOT show any transformer pads, transformer locations, or transformer equipment - no symbols or labels for transformers are visible on this sheet.
reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B requires all electrical plans to be included in the plan set, and Table 1.4.3.A specifies that Electric UG Transformers and Electric OH Transformers must appear on CAD layers. While transformers are shown on the dedicated Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), they must also be shown on the required sheets specified in Table 1.4.3.B, including the landscape plan per the code's requirement to show electric infrastructure on all required sheets. The absence of transformer locations on Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) means the landscape designer has not coordinated around the electrical transformer equipment, creating a potential conflict between landscaping and electrical infrastructure placement.

comment: Electric meter locations must be shown on site plan showing all utilities (Sheet 9) and landscape plan (Sheet 31) in addition to the electrical plan. Add labels identifying the location and number of electrical meters serving each building per UCM § 1.3.4.
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows 8 electrical meter locations, labeled "Electrical Meters" at specific building locations (north wall of Bldg 1, north wall of Bldg 3, east wall of Bldg 5, south wall of Bldg 2, south wall of Bldg 4, east wall of Bldg 6, south wall of Bldg 7, south wall of Bldg 8). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does NOT show any electrical meter locations - despite showing other utilities (water, sewer, storm) and one transformer pad. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does NOT show any electrical meter locations.
reasoning: UCM § 1.3.4 defines the Point of Service and requires its location to be shown. The electrical meter locations are critical to identifying the customer's service equipment and POS. UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires all electrical plans and the site plan showing all utilities and landscape plan to include electric infrastructure. The absence of meter locations on Sheet 9 (Site Plan showing all utilities) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) means these required sheets do not show the complete electric service infrastructure. The customer's service equipment (meters) must be shown on all required plan sheets for proper utility coordination and to verify POS compliance.

comment: Cannot verify whether duct bank routing and locations are required for this project from available evidence. Provide Austin Energy ESPA approval letter, Letter of Agreement for Underground Electric Service, or utility coordination notes confirming whether main line duct banks are required or service-only routing is approved.
observation: Examined Sheet 21 electrical plan which shows underground electric service with standard service lateral conduit routing to each building. The electrical routing appears to show typical service-only conduit sizes (not the 1000 MCM cables in 5-inch conduit that would indicate main line distribution). No Austin Energy ESPA documentation, Letter of Agreement, or utility coordination notes are provided in the supplementary documents that would indicate whether duct banks are required for this project. The Master Comment Report's Electric Review section references Austin Energy design criteria but the actual AE comments are on an external Bluebeam link that cannot be accessed for this review.

Sheet 21 shows what appears to be service-only routing, but without formal AE Design documentation confirming that duct banks are NOT required, the requirement cannot be definitively verified. The absence of AE Design approval documentation in the project file means the applicant may have received AE determinations that are not available in this document set. comment: Cannot verify whether street lighting is required for this site from available evidence. Clarify with Austin Energy Design whether street lighting is required for the Valley View Road frontage per UCM § 1.6.0. If required, show street light layout and pole locations on site plan and landscape plan.

Sheet 9 includes a Lighting Note addressing "exterior lighting" (building wall-mounted lights), not street lighting infrastructure. No street lighting, light poles, or photometric layouts are shown on either sheet. Facts.md indicates Valley View Road is classified as a local street (ASMP Level 1) with existing lane count not on file and a 2-undivided-lane cross-section planned. The site plan does not show street improvements along Valley View Road frontage that would typically trigger street lighting requirements.

The absence of explicit street improvement requirements on Valley View Road frontage and the absence of street lighting from the plans suggest it may not be required. The checklist item states this determination "cannot be determined from plans alone" and must be verified through AE Design coordination, which does not appear to have been completed or documented.

comment: Cannot determine applicability from available evidence. Clarify with Austin Energy Design whether street lighting is required. If required, provide street light conduit plan showing conduit connections and routing on site plan, landscape plan, and all electrical plans per UCM § 1.6.0.
observation: No street light conduit, conduit connections, or conduit routing are shown on Sheet 9 (Site Plan), Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan), or Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan). As noted in EL-17.7 findings, street lighting infrastructure is not visible anywhere in the plan set. The applicability of this item depends on whether street lighting is required, which per UCM § 1.6.0 must be determined by contacting Austin Energy Design.
reasoning: Per the checklist item's applicability note, this item applies "Only when street lighting or parking garage lighting is required." The grouping's regulatory overview (Section 8 of grouping file) states: "Specific street lighting requirements are determined by contacting AE Design (UCM § 1.6.0)." Without documentation of AE Design's determination regarding street lighting applicability, this item's applicability cannot be confirmed. If street lighting is determined to be required by AE Design, then the absence of street light conduit plans would be a deficiency.

comment: Projected electrical load must be shown on plan sheets. Add load calculations table to the electrical design plan showing total projected electrical demand in kW and/or amperes, and breakdown by building if applicable, per UCM § 1.16.0(6).
observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan), Sheet 9 (Site Plan), and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan). No electrical load calculations, demand summaries, amperage requirements, voltage specifications, or load data appear on any of these sheets. No tables or callouts showing projected electrical load for the development (e.g., total kW, total amps, demand load per building) are present. The sheets show physical infrastructure (transformers, meters, lines) but do not quantify the electrical service demand.

This is critical information for Austin Energy to determine service capacity, transformer sizing, and whether line extensions or additional infrastructure are required. The grouping's common violation patterns (item 6 in Description section) lists "Missing projected load: No indication of projected electrical load for the development" as a violation.
